reasons: task is a program with testable logic: the engine and the app are separate deliverables with a clear interface
test-first: a tester item writes tests from the contract, the developer item is graded by tests it did not write
decision: split into 4 items (2 testers, 2 developers)

items.title: Engine tests
items.goal: Write tests for the calculator engine before it exists

card.context: A developer will implement the engine against your tests, so they must be correct and specific.
card.contract: The engine: double calc::evaluate(const std::string& expr, bool degrees = false), declared in include/calc/calc.hpp and defined in src/calc.cpp. Operators: + - * / % ^ (right associative; binds tighter than unary minus, so -2^2 is -4), postfix ! (factorial), parentheses, unary + and -. Numbers: 12, 1.5, .5, 1.5e2. Constants: pi e tau. One-argument functions: sin cos tan asin acos atan sinh cosh tanh ln log (base 10) log2 sqrt cbrt abs exp floor ceil round fact. Two-argument functions: pow min max. degrees=true makes sin cos tan take degrees and asin acos atan return degrees. Invalid input raises the error: division or modulo by zero, unknown names or functions, wrong argument count, sqrt of a negative, unbalanced parentheses, a trailing operator, unexpected characters. Here invalid input raises std::runtime_error.
acceptance: includes "calc/calc.hpp" (engine tests) and "helpers/check.hpp" and defines only TEST cases (CHECK_NEAR, CHECK_EQ, CHECK_THROWS), no main
at least 10 test cases: operators, precedence, ^ associativity, factorial, decimals, constants, radians and degrees, logs, two-argument functions, error cases
floating point results are compared with a tolerance of 1e-9, never with exact equality
tests do not depend on each other

items.title: Expression engine
items.goal: Implement the engine so the provided tests pass

card.context: Replace the stub src/calc.cpp with a real implementation; the tests below are the specification.
card.contract: Implement double calc::evaluate(const std::string& expr, bool degrees = false), declared in include/calc/calc.hpp and defined in src/calc.cpp. Operators: + - * / % ^ (right associative; binds tighter than unary minus, so -2^2 is -4), postfix ! (factorial), parentheses, unary + and -. Numbers: 12, 1.5, .5, 1.5e2. Constants: pi e tau. One-argument functions: sin cos tan asin acos atan sinh cosh tanh ln log (base 10) log2 sqrt cbrt abs exp floor ceil round fact. Two-argument functions: pow min max. degrees=true makes sin cos tan take degrees and asin acos atan return degrees. Raise std::runtime_error with a clear message on any invalid input (Invalid input raises the error: division or modulo by zero, unknown names or functions, wrong argument count, sqrt of a negative, unbalanced parentheses, a trailing operator, unexpected characters.)
acceptance: C++20, standard library only, no warnings
notes: A small recursive descent parser works well: expression -> term -> unary -> postfix -> primary

items.title: App tests
items.goal: Write tests for the calculator command-line app by running it

card.context: A developer will build the app against your tests. The tests run the real program.
card.contract: The app takes an expression as its arguments (joined with spaces) or, with none, one line from standard input. It prints the result with 12 significant digits (%.12g) and a newline and exits 0. On invalid input it prints 'Error: ' and the message to standard error and exits non-zero. --degrees sets degrees mode. --screen prints a fixed frame instead: a line of '+' then 38 '-' then '+', a line '| ' + the expression padded to 36 characters + ' |', a line '| = ' + the result padded to 34 characters + ' |' (an error shows as 'Error: message'), and the first rule line again. In a test, std::string(CALC_CLI_PATH) is the path of the program; run it with popen and read its output.
acceptance: includes "calc/calc.hpp" (engine tests) and "helpers/check.hpp" and defines only TEST cases (CHECK_NEAR, CHECK_EQ, CHECK_THROWS), no main
at least 5 tests: a result, joined arguments, floating point noise (0.1+0.2 prints 0.3), --degrees, an error message with a non-zero exit, and the --screen frame
each test runs the program itself

items.title: Command-line app
items.goal: Write the command-line app so the provided tests pass

card.context: Replace the stub src/main.cpp; the tests below are the specification.
card.contract: int main(int argc, char** argv). The app takes an expression as its arguments (joined with spaces) or, with none, one line from standard input. It prints the result with 12 significant digits (%.12g) and a newline and exits 0. On invalid input it prints 'Error: ' and the message to standard error and exits non-zero. --degrees sets degrees mode. --screen prints a fixed frame instead: a line of '+' then 38 '-' then '+', a line '| ' + the expression padded to 36 characters + ' |', a line '| = ' + the result padded to 34 characters + ' |' (an error shows as 'Error: message'), and the first rule line again. Evaluate with the engine (double calc::evaluate(const std::string& expr, bool degrees = false), declared in include/calc/calc.hpp and defined in src/calc.cpp).
acceptance: C++20, standard library only, no warnings
